chapter_summary: At the Festival of Tabernacles, Jesus teaches publicly despite threats. Crowds and leaders debate His identity and authority. Jesus invites the thirsty to receive living water, which John explains as the Holy Spirit.
main_lesson: Jesus follows the Father’s timing, teaches with divine authority, calls for truthful judgment, and offers the Spirit’s life. The chapter models honest inquiry while exposing coercion, contempt, and unfair judgment.

memory_verse.kjv: In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink.
memory_verse.little_bible: On the last day, the great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried out, saying, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink.”

parent_guide: Access: default ages 9–12 with adult context; selected verses for ages 6–8. Ages 3–5 receive only curated non-conflict verses. Verses 22–23 are 9–12/Parent Mode, adult-led for 6–8, and never standalone for 3–5. Sensitivity: lethal threats, family pressure, secrecy, religious conflict, arrest, authority, circumcision/private-body context, demonic accusation, exclusion, class contempt, and complex Spirit imagery. “Judean leaders/authorities” never means all Jewish people. Private travel never authorizes secret accounts, location concealment, or adult secret demands. Living water is metaphorical and does not replace hydration; the Spirit is not a private voice. In verse 38, both the scriptural source and whether the flow is from the believer or Christ are disputed. In verse 39, the Spirit pre-exists and acts before Jesus’ glorification; Christian traditions explain the promised new-covenant reception differently. John 7:53–8:11 is absent from the earliest surviving manuscripts and appears in varying later locations, making its original placement uncertain; verse 53 also must not imply every child has a conventional safe home.
application_for_children: Children may ask questions, resist unsafe pressure, distinguish privacy from harmful secrets, judge claims carefully with trusted adults, respect Jewish people and neighbours of every belief, protect body privacy, and seek help when threatened or silenced.

verses.kjv: After these things Jesus walked in Galilee: for he would not walk in Jewry, because the Jews sought to kill him.
verses.little_bible: After this, Jesus traveled in Galilee. He would not travel in Judea because the Jews were trying to kill him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus stayed in Galilee because leaders in Judea wanted to kill him.
verses.meaning: Jesus avoids Judea because of a real lethal threat; prudent avoidance is not cowardice.
verses.prayer: Jesus, give me wisdom to choose safety.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about safe choices?
verses.family_discussion: Make a safety plan for avoiding a known threat without calling caution cowardice. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Optionally write two trusted contacts for dangerous situations.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:1, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Now the Jews’ feast of tabernacles was at hand.
verses.little_bible: Now the Jewish Festival of Tabernacles was near.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The Jewish Festival of Tabernacles was near.
verses.meaning: The Feast of Tabernacles provides the chapter’s Jewish setting; explain it respectfully as Israel’s celebration.
verses.prayer: God, thank you for Israel’s festivals and story.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about the festival?
verses.family_discussion: Explore how Tabernacles remembered God’s care, using a reliable Jewish source.
verses.do_it_today: If interested, view an age-appropriate picture of a sukkah.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:2, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: His brethren therefore said unto him, Depart hence, and go into Judaea, that thy disciples also may see the works that thou doest.
verses.little_bible: His brothers therefore said to him, “Leave here and go to Judea, so that your disciples may also see the works you do.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus’ brothers urged him to show his works publicly in Judea.
verses.meaning: Jesus’ brothers pressure him toward publicity without understanding his mission; family pressure need not be obeyed.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help families avoid pressuring one another to perform.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about family pressure?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss why nobody owes family members a public display of talent or faith. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Choose not to perform something simply to prove yourself.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:3, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: For there is no man that doeth any thing in secret, and he himself seeketh to be known openly. If thou do these things, shew thyself to the world.
verses.little_bible: “For no one does anything in secret while seeking to be known openly. If you do these things, show yourself to the world.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They said public recognition required public action.
verses.meaning: Their advice assumes fame requires visibility, but Jesus follows the Father’s timing rather than reputation.
verses.prayer: Jesus, free me from needing public attention.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about public attention?
verses.family_discussion: Name ways families can celebrate gifts without demanding a performance. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Offer someone permission to keep a gift private.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:4, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: For neither did his brethren believe in him.
verses.little_bible: For even his brothers did not believe in him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: His brothers did not believe.
verses.meaning: The brothers’ unbelief shows family closeness does not guarantee faith; it does not justify shaming relatives.
verses.prayer: God, meet families where belief is difficult.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about family unbelief?
verses.family_discussion: Reassure one another that family disagreement does not cancel belonging. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Listen kindly to a relative who questions, or pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:5, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Then Jesus said unto them, My time is not yet come: but your time is alway ready.
verses.little_bible: Then Jesus said to them, “My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said their time was always ready, but his time had not yet come.
verses.meaning: Jesus distinguishes his appointed time from theirs; this concerns his unique mission, not secret timing messages to children.
verses.prayer: Jesus, teach me patience with your timing.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about God’s timing?
verses.family_discussion: Compare patient timing with giving in to family pressure. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Wait before one non-urgent decision.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:6, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: The world cannot hate you; but me it hateth, because I testify of it, that the works thereof are evil.
verses.little_bible: “The world cannot hate you, but it hates me because I testify that its works are evil.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The world did not hate them, but hated Jesus because he exposed evil.
verses.meaning: Jesus’ truthful witness exposes evil and draws hostility; children should not seek conflict or assume disagreement proves righteousness.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me speak truth without seeking hostility.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about truth and hostility?
verses.family_discussion: Ask how truth can be spoken without deliberately provoking danger. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Use one truthful sentence that does not insult anyone.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:7, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Go ye up unto this feast: I go not up yet unto this feast; for my time is not yet full come.
verses.little_bible: “Go up to this feast. I am not yet going up to this feast, because my time has not yet fully come.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus told his brothers to attend; he would not go then because his time was not complete.
verses.meaning: Jesus declines their proposed plan; his words concern timing, not deceptive secrecy.
verses.prayer: God, guide me toward wise and honest boundaries.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about wise boundaries?
verses.family_discussion: Practise declining a pressured invitation respectfully. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Practise saying, “No, that plan is not right for me.”
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:8, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: When he had said these words unto them, he abode still in Galilee.
verses.little_bible: When he had said these words to them, he remained in Galilee.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: After saying this, Jesus remained in Galilee.
verses.meaning: Jesus stays in Galilee after the conversation, maintaining his stated decision at that moment.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me wait without fear.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about patient waiting?
verses.family_discussion: Talk about waiting after making a wise decision.
verses.do_it_today: Take no action; notice Jesus remains where he is.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:9, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: But when his brethren were gone up, then went he also up unto the feast, not openly, but as it were in secret.
verses.little_bible: But after his brothers had gone to the feast, he also went, not openly, but as if in secret.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: After his brothers left, Jesus also went to the festival privately.
verses.meaning: Jesus later travels privately, not as a public display. Privacy for safety differs from adults demanding secret-keeping from children. This privacy never permits secret travel, hidden accounts, concealed location sharing, or an adult demanding that a child keep unsafe secrets.
verses.prayer: God, help me value privacy without hiding danger.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about privacy and secrecy?
verses.family_discussion: Compare healthy privacy with an adult demanding harmful secrecy. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: With an adult, repeat: “Unsafe secrets must be told.”
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:10, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Then the Jews sought him at the feast, and said, Where is he?
verses.little_bible: Then the Jews looked for him at the feast and asked, “Where is he?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jewish leaders looked for Jesus at the festival.
verses.meaning: Leaders seek Jesus amid conflict. “The Jews” in this Gospel often means particular Judean authorities, never all Jewish people.
verses.prayer: Jesus, give leaders humility when they seek answers.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about specific leaders?
verses.family_discussion: Notice which particular leaders are searching and avoid blaming a whole people.
verses.do_it_today: Underline the specific group named in the adaptation.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:11, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: And there was much murmuring among the people concerning him: for some said, He is a good man: others said, Nay; but he deceiveth the people.
verses.little_bible: And there was much whispering among the people about him, for some said, “He is a good man.” Others said, “No, but he deceives the people.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Crowds quietly debated whether Jesus was good or deceptive.
verses.meaning: Crowds disagree about Jesus. Honest evaluation differs from contemptuous labeling.
verses.prayer: God, help me consider claims fairly.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about different opinions?
verses.family_discussion: Let different family members explain what evidence they would examine.
verses.do_it_today: List two kinds of evidence people might consider.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:12, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Howbeit no man spake openly of him for fear of the Jews.
verses.little_bible: However, no one spoke openly about him because they feared the Jews.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Fear kept people from speaking openly.
verses.meaning: Fear of authorities suppresses public speech; children should tell safe adults when intimidation silences them.
verses.prayer: God, give courage and safe help when authority intimidates.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about fear and speech?
verses.family_discussion: Plan whom a child can tell when authority makes speaking feel unsafe. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Name a safe reporting route, without sharing an incident.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:13, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Now about the midst of the feast Jesus went up into the temple, and taught.
verses.little_bible: Now about halfway through the feast, Jesus went into the temple and taught.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Halfway through the festival, Jesus taught in the temple.
verses.meaning: Jesus begins public temple teaching midway through the festival.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me listen carefully to your teaching.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about Jesus teaching?
verses.family_discussion: Consider why Jesus chose this moment and place to teach.
verses.do_it_today: Listen to the verse once more in its festival setting.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:14, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: And the Jews marvelled, saying, How knoweth this man letters, having never learned?
verses.little_bible: And the Jews were amazed, saying, “How does this man know the writings, having never studied?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: People wondered how Jesus knew Scripture without their formal training.
verses.meaning: Listeners marvel at Jesus’ knowledge despite lacking their recognized rabbinic training.
verses.prayer: God, help me value truth beyond credentials.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about learning and authority?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss when training helps and when people wrongly dismiss an uncredentialed speaker.
verses.do_it_today: Thank a teacher without treating credentials as proof of truth.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:15, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Jesus answered them, and said, My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me.
verses.little_bible: Jesus answered them, “My teaching is not mine, but belongs to the one who sent me.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said his teaching came from the one who sent him.
verses.meaning: Jesus locates his teaching’s authority in the Father who sent him, not self-promotion.
verses.prayer: Father, help me receive what you teach through Jesus.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about the teaching’s source?
verses.family_discussion: Trace how Jesus identifies the source of his teaching.
verses.do_it_today: Mark the words showing who sent Jesus.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:16, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself.
verses.little_bible: “If anyone wants to do his will, he will know whether the teaching is from God or whether I speak from myself.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A person willing to do God’s will could recognize the teaching’s source.
verses.meaning: Willingness to do God’s will helps discern Jesus’ teaching; this is not permission to manipulate uncertain children.
verses.prayer: God, shape my willingness without coercion.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about discernment?
verses.family_discussion: Explore willingness and discernment without forcing anyone to claim certainty.
verses.do_it_today: Ask one question freely, with no required answer.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:17, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: He that speaketh of himself seeketh his own glory: but he that seeketh his glory that sent him, the same is true, and no unrighteousness is in him.
verses.little_bible: “The one who speaks from himself seeks his own glory. But the one who seeks the glory of the one who sent him is true, and there is nothing wrong in him.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Speaking from oneself seeks personal glory. Seeking the Sender’s glory is truthful, with no unrighteousness.
verses.meaning: Seeking God’s glory marks truthful mission, while self-glory distorts teaching. Leaders still require accountability.
verses.prayer: God, turn my attention from self-glory to your truth.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about God’s glory?
verses.family_discussion: Compare seeking personal applause with seeking the Sender’s honour.
verses.do_it_today: Do one useful task without seeking public credit.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:18, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Did not Moses give you the law, and yet none of you keepeth the law? Why go ye about to kill me?
verses.little_bible: “Did not Moses give you the law? Yet none of you keeps the law. Why do you seek to kill me?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said Moses gave the law, yet none kept it, and asked why they sought to kill him.
verses.meaning: Jesus exposes hypocrisy regarding Moses’ law and the plot against him. This accusation targets the present opponents, not Jewish people generally.
verses.prayer: God, expose hypocrisy without making me cruel.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about law and hypocrisy?
verses.family_discussion: Ask why law knowledge does not excuse plotting harm. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Leave judgment of threats to responsible adults and seek help.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:19, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: The people answered and said, Thou hast a devil: who goeth about to kill thee?
verses.little_bible: The people answered, “You have a demon! Who is seeking to kill you?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The crowd claimed Jesus had a demon and denied seeking his death.
verses.meaning: Some in the crowd misunderstand or deny the threat and accuse Jesus of demonic influence. Do not dramatize this to frighten children. Demon language must never label mental illness, disability, distress, intrusive thoughts, or unfamiliar behaviour.
verses.prayer: Jesus, protect people from harmful labels.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about misunderstanding?
verses.family_discussion: State why distress, disability, mental illness, or unusual thoughts must never be called demonic. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Replace one harmful label with respectful care language.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:20, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Jesus answered and said unto them, I have done one work, and ye all marvel.
verses.little_bible: Jesus answered them, “I have done one work, and you are all amazed.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said one work had amazed them.
verses.meaning: The “one work” refers to Jesus’ Sabbath healing that astonished and angered observers.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me understand your healing work.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about the Sabbath work?
verses.family_discussion: Look back at the healing story that caused the amazement. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Revisit the earlier healing passage if you wish.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:21, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Moses therefore gave unto you circumcision; (not because it is of Moses, but of the fathers;) and ye on the sabbath day circumcise a man.
verses.little_bible: “Moses therefore gave you circumcision—not because it came from Moses, but from the ancestors—and you circumcise a male on the Sabbath day.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said circumcision came through the ancestors and was performed on the Sabbath.
verses.meaning: Jesus notes circumcision’s ancestral origin and Sabbath practice. It is an ancient procedure involving a boy’s private area. Discussion is 9–12/Parent Mode, clinical and non-graphic, led by a safe caregiver; no child is asked about their body, shown imagery, examined, or told to keep any body-related secret.
verses.prayer: God, protect every child’s body and privacy.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about circumcision and privacy?
verses.family_discussion: An adult may explain the ancient practice while affirming private-body safety; no child shares body details. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: No child action: adults protect body privacy and answer questions clinically.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:22, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: If a man on the sabbath day receive circumcision, that the law of Moses should not be broken; are ye angry at me, because I have made a man every whit whole on the sabbath day?
verses.little_bible: “If a male receives circumcision on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses should not be broken, are you angry with me because I made a man completely well on the Sabbath?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: If circumcision could occur on Sabbath, they should not be angry that Jesus healed a whole person.
verses.meaning: Jesus argues from accepted Sabbath circumcision to the rightness of making a whole person well. Keep body details private and adult-led. “Whole” describes comprehensive healing, not greater bodily value; disabled and unhealed people retain equal dignity.
verses.prayer: Jesus, thank you for valuing the whole person.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about healing a whole person?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss why healing a whole person does not rank some bodies as more valuable. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Celebrate a person without discussing their body or abilities.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:23, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.
verses.little_bible: “Do not judge by appearance, but judge with right judgment.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus told them not to judge by appearance but to judge rightly.
verses.meaning: Jesus commands judgment according to truth rather than surface appearance; this does not grant children judicial authority. Children should report concerns to trusted adults, not judge people, confront suspects, or investigate.
verses.prayer: God, teach us truth and fair judgment.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about fair judgment?
verses.family_discussion: Practise checking appearances while leaving investigation to safe trained adults.
verses.do_it_today: Report concern to an adult rather than investigating it yourself.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:24, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Then said some of them of Jerusalem, Is not this he, whom they seek to kill?
verses.little_bible: Then some people from Jerusalem said, “Is this not the man they are seeking to kill?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: People recognized the man leaders sought.
verses.meaning: Jerusalem residents recognize the known effort to kill Jesus. Threats should be named and reported, not normalized.
verses.prayer: God, give threatened people wise help.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about recognized danger?
verses.family_discussion: Identify safe help when a known threat is discussed publicly. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Move toward a trusted adult if a threat appears, or pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:25, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: But, lo, he speaketh boldly, and they say nothing unto him. Do the rulers know indeed that this is the very Christ?
verses.little_bible: “But look, he speaks boldly, and they say nothing to him. Do the rulers truly know that this is the Christ?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus spoke openly, yet leaders said nothing; people wondered if rulers knew he was Christ.
verses.meaning: Jesus’ open teaching and leaders’ inaction create public uncertainty about their judgment.
verses.prayer: Jesus, guide people who are uncertain about you.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about public uncertainty?
verses.family_discussion: Talk about why leaders’ silence can be interpreted in different ways.
verses.do_it_today: Hold one conclusion lightly while gathering facts.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:26, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Howbeit we know this man whence he is: but when Christ cometh, no man knoweth whence he is.
verses.little_bible: “However, we know where this man comes from. But when the Christ comes, no one will know where he comes from.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They thought they knew where Jesus came from, but believed no one would know the Christ’s origin.
verses.meaning: The crowd thinks it knows where Jesus comes from, while expecting Messiah’s source to be unknown. The claim concerns origin, not merely present location, and reflects debated expectations.
verses.prayer: God, help me examine assumptions about Jesus.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about human origins?
verses.family_discussion: Compare knowing where someone comes from with understanding who sent them.
verses.do_it_today: Correct the adaptation’s “origin” language by noticing who sent Jesus.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:27, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Then cried Jesus in the temple as he taught, saying, Ye both know me, and ye know whence I am: and I am not come of myself, but he that sent me is true, whom ye know not.
verses.little_bible: Then Jesus cried out while teaching in the temple, “You know me, and you know where I come from. I have not come from myself, but the one who sent me is true, and you do not know him.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said he did not come by himself; the truthful Sender was unknown to them.
verses.meaning: Jesus acknowledges their familiarity while insisting his mission comes from the truthful Father whom they do not know.
verses.prayer: Father, thank you for sending Jesus truthfully.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about the Father who sent Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Explore why Jesus says the truthful Father was unknown to his opponents.
verses.do_it_today: Circle the descriptions of the Sender.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:28, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: But I know him: for I am from him, and he hath sent me.
verses.little_bible: “But I know him: for I am from him, and he has sent me.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus knew the Father who sent him.
verses.meaning: Jesus uniquely knows the Father because he comes from and is sent by him; this claim is not a private-voice model.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me know the Father through you.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about Jesus knowing Father?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss Jesus’ unique knowledge without treating private thoughts as divine messages.
verses.do_it_today: Listen for what Jesus uniquely claims about the Father.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:29, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Then they sought to take him: but no man laid hands on him, because his hour was not yet come.
verses.little_bible: Then they sought to seize him, but no one laid hands on him because his hour had not yet come.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They tried to arrest Jesus, but no one seized him because his hour had not come.
verses.meaning: The attempted arrest fails within John’s theology of Jesus’ appointed hour. It does not promise believers supernatural escape from arrest or harm.
verses.prayer: God, protect people facing unjust arrest.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about arrest and Jesus’ hour?
verses.family_discussion: Review that failed arrest here never promises escape from harm. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: No risky action; remember that safety help is still needed.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:30, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: And many of the people believed on him, and said, When Christ cometh, will he do more miracles than these which this man hath done?
verses.little_bible: And many among the people believed in him and said, “When the Christ comes, will he do more miracles than this man has done?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Many believed and asked whether Christ would do more signs than Jesus.
verses.meaning: Many evaluate Jesus by his signs and conclude no expected Messiah could surpass them.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me respond honestly to your signs.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about signs and belief?
verses.family_discussion: Ask whether signs alone answer every question about Jesus.
verses.do_it_today: Compare one sign with Jesus’ teaching.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:31, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: The Pharisees heard that the people murmured such things concerning him; and the Pharisees and the chief priests sent officers to take him.
verses.little_bible: The Pharisees heard the people whispering these things about him, and the Pharisees and chief priests sent officers to seize him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Pharisees heard the crowd; chief priests and Pharisees sent officers to arrest Jesus.
verses.meaning: Religious leaders coordinate an arrest after hearing growing public belief. Avoid presenting all Pharisees or Jews as identical.
verses.prayer: God, restrain leaders who misuse authority.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about religious power?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss how religious and state-like authority can be accountable. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Write one respectful question for a leader.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:32, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Then said Jesus unto them, Yet a little while am I with you, and then I go unto him that sent me.
verses.little_bible: Then Jesus said to them, “I am with you for a little while longer, and then I go to the one who sent me.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said he would remain a little longer, then return to the one who sent him.
verses.meaning: Jesus predicts his limited remaining time and return to the Father through death, resurrection, and ascension.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me trust your mission and timing.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about Jesus’ departure?
verses.family_discussion: Name how departure language points toward death, resurrection, and return to the Father. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Place departure events in order with adult help.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:33, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me: and where I am, thither ye cannot come.
verses.little_bible: “You will seek me, and will not find me: and where I am, there you cannot come.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They would seek him but not find him, and could not come where he was.
verses.meaning: Jesus warns opponents they will miss access to him. It is a serious consequence, not a threat for controlling children.
verses.prayer: God, help me hear serious warnings without manipulation.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about a serious warning?
verses.family_discussion: Read the warning calmly without using it to frighten someone into belief. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Pause or skip if the warning feels frightening.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:34, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Then said the Jews among themselves, Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?
verses.little_bible: Then the Jews said among themselves, “Where will he go that we will not find him? Will he go to those scattered among the Gentiles and teach the Gentiles?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Leaders wondered whether Jesus would go teach dispersed Jewish people and Greeks.
verses.meaning: Leaders speculate he might teach Jewish communities dispersed among Greeks. The verse reflects a diverse Jewish diaspora.
verses.prayer: God, help us respect peoples and cultures we discuss.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about the Jewish diaspora?
verses.family_discussion: Locate Jewish diaspora communities and Greeks without stereotypes. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Find one diaspora location on a map with an adult.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:35, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: What manner of saying is this that he said, Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me: and where I am, thither ye cannot come?
verses.little_bible: “What does this saying mean: ‘You will seek me and will not find me, and where I am, you cannot come’?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They wondered what Jesus meant about seeking, not finding, and being unable to come.
verses.meaning: Their repeated question shows unresolved misunderstanding of Jesus’ departure.
verses.prayer: Jesus, welcome my questions when I do not understand.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about unanswered questions?
verses.family_discussion: Welcome unresolved questions rather than pretending the leaders understood. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Add an unanswered question to a family question box.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:36, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink.
verses.little_bible: On the last day, the great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried out, saying, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: On the festival’s final great day, Jesus invited thirsty people to come and drink.
verses.meaning: During the water ceremony’s festival climax, Jesus publicly invites spiritually thirsty people to come to him and drink. Spiritual thirst never replaces ordinary hydration; children must drink safe water and seek medical help when needed.
verses.prayer: Jesus, meet spiritual thirst and remind us to drink water.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about spiritual thirst?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss spiritual thirst, then remember ordinary bodies still need safe drinking water.
verses.do_it_today: Drink ordinary safe water, then hear Jesus’ metaphor again.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:37, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.
verses.little_bible: “The one who believes in me, as the Scripture has said, from inside him will flow rivers of living water.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said believers would have rivers of living water flowing from within.
verses.meaning: Living water is a metaphor for abundant Spirit-given life, not literal water inside bodies or guaranteed feelings. The flow’s referent—believer or Christ—and the claimed scriptural background are disputed; no single Old Testament quotation exactly matches the wording.
verses.prayer: Jesus, give the life your living-water image describes.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about living water?
verses.family_discussion: Compare metaphorical living water with literal fluid; avoid body speculation.
verses.do_it_today: Draw a river as a symbol, not something inside a body.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:38, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: (But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive: for the Holy Ghost was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified.)
verses.little_bible: (But he spoke this about the Spirit, whom those who believe in him should receive. For the Holy Spirit was not yet given, because Jesus was not yet glorified.)
verses.little_reader_adaptation: John explains Jesus meant the Spirit, whom believers would receive after Jesus was glorified.
verses.meaning: John interprets the living water as the Holy Spirit, given after Jesus’ glorification. The personal Spirit is not a private voice children must obey. The Spirit existed and acted before this moment; traditions distinguish pre-glorification activity from promised new-covenant reception differently. This is not literal body fluid or a private voice children must obey.
verses.prayer: Holy Spirit, center my attention on Jesus and Scripture.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about the Holy Spirit?
verses.family_discussion: Read the surrounding verses and discuss whether the river flows from believer or Christ; note faithful readers differ. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Check a spiritual claim against Scripture and trusted adults.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:39, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Many of the people therefore, when they heard this saying, said, Of a truth this is the Prophet.
verses.little_bible: Many among the people therefore, when they heard this saying, said, “Truly, this is the Prophet.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Some who heard said Jesus truly was the Prophet.
verses.meaning: Some identify Jesus as the promised prophet, showing one response within the divided crowd.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me consider the crowd’s claim carefully.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about the Prophet?
verses.family_discussion: What did people mean by calling Jesus ‘the Prophet,’ and what evidence were they considering?
verses.do_it_today: Make no action demand; listen to the explanation if ready.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:40, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Others said, This is the Christ. But some said, Shall Christ come out of Galilee?
verses.little_bible: Others said, “This is the Christ.” But some asked, “Will the Christ come from Galilee?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Others said he was Christ; some questioned whether Christ came from Galilee.
verses.meaning: Others debate Messiah and Galilee. Geographic assumptions shape their disagreement but do not settle Jesus’ identity.
verses.prayer: God, guide honest questions about Messiah.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about Messiah and Galilee?
verses.family_discussion: What geographic assumption did some people make about the Messiah, and why should a region never determine a person’s dignity?
verses.do_it_today: Look up the promised prophet with an older reader.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:41, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Hath not the scripture said, That Christ cometh of the seed of David, and out of the town of Bethlehem, where David was?
verses.little_bible: “Has not the Scripture said that the Christ comes from David’s descendants and from Bethlehem, the town where David lived?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They cited Scripture that Christ came from David’s family and Bethlehem.
verses.meaning: They appeal to Scripture concerning Davidic descent and Bethlehem, unaware of or not discussing Jesus’ birth tradition.
verses.prayer: God, help me read Scripture carefully and humbly.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about Scripture and Bethlehem?
verses.family_discussion: What did Scripture say about David’s family and Bethlehem, and what information about Jesus might the crowd have lacked?
verses.do_it_today: Mark Bethlehem and Galilee on a map without judging people by region.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:42, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: So there was a division among the people because of him.
verses.little_bible: So there was a division among the people because of him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The crowd was divided because of Jesus.
verses.meaning: The crowd divides over Jesus; disagreement itself neither proves nor disproves truth.
verses.prayer: Jesus, teach divided people truth with respect.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about division?
verses.family_discussion: How can people disagree about an important belief without insults, threats, or pressure? You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Read one source about Jesus’ birth with an adult.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:43, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: And some of them would have taken him; but no man laid hands on him.
verses.little_bible: And some of them wanted to seize him, but no one laid hands on him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Some wanted to arrest him, but no one seized him.
verses.meaning: Some intend arrest, yet it does not occur. Again, this is not a universal safety promise.
verses.prayer: God, protect people from unjust seizure.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about failed arrest?
verses.family_discussion: Wanting to seize someone is not ordinary disagreement. What safe adult help is needed when conflict becomes a threat? You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Let two people disagree without making either a villain.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:44, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Then came the officers to the chief priests and Pharisees; and they said unto them, Why have ye not brought him?
verses.little_bible: Then the officers came to the chief priests and Pharisees, who asked them, “Why have you not brought him?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Officers returned without Jesus; leaders asked why.
verses.meaning: Temple officers return without carrying out the arrest order.
verses.prayer: God, give public servants courage and wisdom.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about the officers’ return?
verses.family_discussion: Review how to respond if an authority orders something unjust or unsafe. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Tell a safe adult if an authority requests harm or secrecy.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:45, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: The officers answered, Never man spake like this man.
verses.little_bible: The officers answered, “No one ever spoke like this man.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The officers praised Jesus’ speech.
verses.meaning: The officers are struck by Jesus’ unmatched speech.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me listen to your remarkable words.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about Jesus’ words?
verses.family_discussion: Ask why the officers’ firsthand hearing challenged their orders.
verses.do_it_today: Read the officers’ sentence aloud: “No one spoke like this.”
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:46, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Then answered them the Pharisees, Are ye also deceived?
verses.little_bible: Then the Pharisees answered them, “Are you also deceived?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Pharisees accused the officers.
verses.meaning: Pharisees respond with suspicion and accuse the officers of deception rather than investigating fairly.
verses.prayer: God, help authorities question themselves fairly.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about accusations of deception?
verses.family_discussion: Practise an authority figure asking, “Could I be mistaken?” You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: A leader may write one way they could welcome correction.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:47, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Have any of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed on him?
verses.little_bible: “Have any of the rulers or Pharisees believed in him?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They asked whether any ruler believed.
verses.meaning: Their appeal to elite unbelief assumes leaders determine truth; authority and expertise deserve hearing but are not infallible.
verses.prayer: God, keep expertise humble and accountable.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about elite authority?
verses.family_discussion: Compare expert knowledge with infallibility; neither rulers nor religious teachers are beyond review. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Ask who is missing from an authority’s decision.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:48, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: But this people who knoweth not the law are cursed.
verses.little_bible: “But these people who do not know the law are cursed.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They called the law-ignorant crowd cursed.
verses.meaning: The leaders contemptuously dismiss ordinary people as ignorant and cursed. The narrative exposes class contempt; it does not endorse it. The crowd retains full human dignity; education or status never determines worth.
verses.prayer: God, defend the dignity of people treated with contempt.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about class contempt?
verses.family_discussion: Correct the crowd insult by naming each person’s equal dignity. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Say aloud, “Knowledge does not determine human worth.”
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:49, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Nicodemus saith unto them, (he that came to Jesus by night, being one of them,)
verses.little_bible: Nicodemus—who had come to Jesus by night and was one of them—said to them,
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Nicodemus, who had visited Jesus at night, was among them.
verses.meaning: Nicodemus is identified as a Pharisee and earlier visitor, preventing an anti-Pharisee stereotype.
verses.prayer: God, give cautious voices courage to seek fairness.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about Nicodemus?
verses.family_discussion: Notice how Nicodemus participates in the group yet questions its rush. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Notice one person who questions their own group fairly.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:50, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Doth our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he doeth?
verses.little_bible: “Does our law judge anyone before it hears him and learns what he does?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Nicodemus asked for a fair hearing.
verses.meaning: Nicodemus appeals to lawful procedure: hear a person and learn the facts before judgment. Fair process protects against mob certainty. A child reports what they experienced; trained, safe adults are responsible for investigation and judgment.
verses.prayer: God, help trained adults investigate reports justly.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about fair hearing?
verses.family_discussion: Role-play a child reporting concern while trained adults—not the child—investigate facts. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Practise: “I need to report; adults will investigate.”
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:51, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: They answered and said unto him, Art thou also of Galilee? Search, and look: for out of Galilee ariseth no prophet.
verses.little_bible: They answered him, “Are you also from Galilee? Search and see, for no prophet arises from Galilee.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They mocked Nicodemus as Galilean and claimed no prophet arose from Galilee.
verses.meaning: The reply uses Galilean origin as ridicule and overstates the evidence: Jonah came from Gath-hepher in Galilee, and some manuscripts read “the prophet” while others read “a prophet.” Prejudice and careless research undermine their claim.
verses.prayer: God, uncover prejudice and correct careless claims.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about regional mockery?
verses.family_discussion: Check the Jonah-from-Galilee issue and manuscript variation; discuss how prejudice weakened the reply. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: With an adult, check Jonah 1:1 and 2 Kings 14:25.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:52, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.

verses.kjv: And every man went unto his own house.
verses.little_bible: And each person went to his own house.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Everyone then went home.
verses.meaning: John 7:53 begins the passage commonly extending through 8:11. It is absent from the earliest surviving manuscripts and appears at different locations in some later manuscripts, so its original placement is uncertain. “Everyone went home” closes the scene but must not assume every child has a conventional or safe home.
verses.prayer: God, guide us through difficult manuscript questions.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse help us notice about the scene’s ending?
verses.family_discussion: Explain that 7:53–8:11 is absent from the earliest manuscripts and its original location is uncertain; do not assume every person has a safe home. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: No required action; an older reader may compare Bible footnotes.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 7:53, historically appropriate Jewish festival setting, culturally accurate clothing, gentle non-graphic composition, no text.
